rbit's own: publish or recover one pull request for a pair of branches
post.description: `schema: rbit.pr-ensure/1`. Body: `head` (branch or `owner:branch`), `base`, optional `title`, `body`, `draft` (default `true`) and `request_id`. An open pull request from the same head into the same base is returned (`200`, `outcome: existing`) instead of refused. With `request_id`, the answer is remembered for a week: a retry with the same inputs returns the same pull request (`200`, `outcome: replayed`), even if the first call's response was lost; reusing the id with other inputs is `409 conflict`. A new pull request is `201`, `outcome: created`. Answers `number`, `outcome` and the `pull` as `GET …/pulls/{number}` shows it.

201.description: A new pull request (an existing or replayed one answers 200)

get.summary: rbit's own: whether the head can merge, by the merge's own rules
get.description: `schema: rbit.readiness/1`: the evaluation the merge itself runs (and the merge box shows), for the current head: `ready`, `blocked` (a protection rule is unmet), `may_bypass`, each requirement (`name`, `met`, `says`, `protection`), and each status context: the required ones as `expected` (nothing reported yet), `running`, `failed` or `passed`, and the others with `required: false`. A required check no workflow will report for this head (filtered out, skip marker) is not required. With `head`, a different current head is `409 head_changed`.

parameters.name: head
parameters.description: The head the caller expects (a full id or a prefix).

post.summary: rbit's own: mark a draft ready for review, for an exact head
post.description: Body: `head`, the head the caller expects. A draft is marked ready for review (as the web page's button does); a pull request already ready is left alone. A different current head is `409 head_changed`. Answers the readiness, as `GET …/readiness` does. Needs a `write` token, and the author or a writer.

200.description: The readiness after marking it ready

get.summary: rbit's own: merge base, ahead and behind, without a diff
get.description: `schema: rbit.compare/1`: the full ids of `base` and `head`, their best common ancestor (`null` for unrelated histories), and the commits each has that the other has not (`ahead`, `behind`, counted up to 10,000).

get.summary: rbit's own: whether a branch contains a commit
get.description: `schema: rbit.contains/1`: whether `ref` (the default branch when not given) is `commit` or has it as an ancestor, with the commit's full id.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The branch, tag or commit that may contain it; the default branch when not given.

parameters.name: sha
parameters.description: A commit id, branch or tag

get.summary: rbit's own: the pull requests a commit belongs to
get.description: `schema: rbit.commit-pulls/1`: the pull requests whose head is the commit, that merged as it, or that merged it as their head, open, closed or merged, newest first, at most 50: `number`, `title`, `state` (`open`, `closed`, `merged`), `role` (`head`, `merge_commit`, `merged_head`), `base` and `head_branch`.

post.summary: rbit's own: queue a pull request to land only after its merge passed CI
post.description: Body: `head` (the head the caller expects; a different one is `409 head_changed`) and `merge_method` (`merge`, `squash` or `rebase`). Every requirement but the checks must be met now (`405` otherwise, saying which). One pull request per line is tested at a time: its merge on the current base tip is built into `refs/merge-queue/<base>/pr-<n>`, which workflows see as a push to the branch `merge-queue/<base>/pr-<n>`. When every context the base's protection requires has passed on that commit, exactly that commit becomes the base by compare-and-swap; a base that moved meanwhile means a new candidate and a new test, so nothing lands untested. A failed required check, a conflict or a moved head takes it out of line with the reason. `schema: rbit.queue/1`: `state` (`waiting`, `testing`, `landed`, `failed`, `removed`), `position` in line (1 is being tested or next; `null` once out of line), the queued `head`, `base`, `merge_method`, the `candidate` commit and the base tip it was `built_on`, `attempts` and, after leaving the line, the `reason`.

get.summary: rbit's own: a pull request's place in the merge queue
get.description: The newest queue entry of the pull request, in line or not. `schema: rbit.queue/1`: `state` (`waiting`, `testing`, `landed`, `failed`, `removed`), `position` in line (1 is being tested or next; `null` once out of line), the queued `head`, `base`, `merge_method`, the `candidate` commit and the base tip it was `built_on`, `attempts` and, after leaving the line, the `reason`.

delete.summary: rbit's own: take a pull request out of the merge queue
delete.description: Takes the pull request out of line and deletes its candidate; `404` when it was not in line. Needs a `write` token.

post.summary: rbit's own: merge the base into a pull request's head branch
post.description: `schema: rbit.update-branch/1`. Body: `expected_head`, the head the caller saw (`409 head_changed` otherwise). Merges the base tip into the head branch with a merge commit by the caller, through branch protection as a push would (`405` with the reason when refused), and reports it as a push. Answers the new `head` and whether it moved (`updated`; an up-to-date head is left alone). Only head branches in the same repository.

post.summary: rbit's own: revert a commit into a ready-made pull request
post.description: `schema: rbit.revert/1`. Body: `commit` and `base` (the default branch when not given). Makes branch `revert-<first 12 digits of the commit>` from the base tip with one commit that undoes the commit, and opens a pull request for it into the base; it never merges on its own. `405` with the reason when the revert conflicts, the change is no longer there, or the branch exists.

post.summary: rbit's own: move a branch by compare-and-swap
post.description: `schema: rbit.branch-update/1`. Body: `branch`, `sha` and `expected` (full commit ids). Moves the branch from `expected` to `sha` if a push by the caller would be allowed (`405` with the reason otherwise), atomically: `409 head_changed` when the branch is no longer `expected`. Reported as a push.

title.description: Defaults to the single commit's summary or the branch name.

patch.description: Unified diff hunks; null for binary or very large files.

sha.description: The head the caller reviewed; a different head is a 409.

in_reply_to.description: Reply to this comment (path and line are then taken from it).
